# Workflow checkpoints — complete instructions and evidence of application

These are substeps of the existing workflow, not new phases or human gates. Preserve scope, professional review, local exclusions, schedules and the Phase 0 approval. A delivery log proves only that text was emitted; it does not prove comprehension, correct application, independent review or permission to publish.

## Startup and complete reading

Run `bash .claude/tools/workflow-start.sh` directly as a standalone command (add `--cloud` in cloud). Inspect its actual exit status. Never pipe it through `tail`, `head`, `tee` or another command, chain past failure, or treat a checkbox as proof. The wrapper's internal pipefail cannot protect its caller's pipeline. Startup returns a fresh `runId` after verification. Pass that exact ID via `--run-id <runId>` to subsequent startup checks and every `workflow-preflight.py prepare` in this same routine. Never reuse a previous routine's ID, including when starting another routine in the same chat. Runners may instead supply a fresh per-invocation `WORKFLOW_RUN_ID` consistently in their environment. For the legacy standards loader, use `WORKFLOW_RUN_ID=<runId> bash .claude/tools/load-standards.sh <routine> <phase>` so its internal startup continues the same verified run. This preserves this run's edits without carrying exemptions into later routines.

Before chart research/planning, substantive writing/enrichment, independent audit and publication, prepare the applicable instruction bundle:

```bash
python3 .claude/tools/workflow-preflight.py prepare --run-id <runId> --phase build --actor <agent-id> --instruction .claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-build-brief.md --run-dir reports/mindmap-pass/<run-id>/preflight-build
python3 .claude/tools/workflow-preflight.py next --run-dir reports/mindmap-pass/<run-id>/preflight-build
python3 .claude/tools/workflow-preflight.py check --run-dir reports/mindmap-pass/<run-id>/preflight-build
```

Use `write`, `audit` or `publish` and the actual current phase file at the corresponding existing checkpoint. Other content routines supply their own phase instruction; repeat `--instruction` for additional caller rules. Cloud prepare also takes `--cloud`. Use a unique directory per run, actor and phase. Preparation runs startup verification internally and stops on its real return code. Missing required files block the affected work; global routines must first install the sibling shared contracts/helper into the active project while preserving its local standards and permissions.

Run `next` **once per tool call**, read that complete chunk, then repeat until all chunks are read. Do not batch outputs, pipe/truncate them, use byte counts/head excerpts as reading, or summarize an unread source. If the tool itself truncates a result, reread that part with `--part N` before advancing. `check` must succeed before dependent work; it rejects incomplete delivery, changed chunks, changed source files and newly added local overrides. If rules change, prepare/read a fresh bundle and reconcile already prepared artifacts. The independent reviewer loads its own audit bundle; it cannot inherit the writer's reading claim. To avoid repeatedly loading unchanged rules, the same actor in the same run may pass `--reuse <completed-earlier-bundle>` to prepare the next phase. The helper validates the earlier delivery and source hashes, then emits only new files (normally the next phase instructions). Use your actual distinct agent identity in `--actor`; independent reviewers start their own bundle and never reuse the writer’s. Reuse is not valid across a new chat or lost reading context. If context no longer contains the rules, reread them. This complete-reading protocol supersedes older directions to use only `load-standards.sh`. Its legacy ledger receipt is still allowed for compatibility, but is not a substitute for these checks and does not require a second reading of unchanged rules.

Record a concise application map in the existing run notes: exact source hashes from the bundle, this site's permissions/exclusions/review obligations, applicable reader/evidence/takeaway/label rules, and the artifact or concrete decision that implements each. Use an explicit reason for genuinely inapplicable rules. A list of rule names or yes/no ticks without evidence does not pass review. Do not fabricate evidence merely to fill a field.

## Chart gate: discovery coverage and relevance

The existing independent chart reviewer verifies the build bundle check and application map, then checks saved raw keyword results, not only the author's conclusions:
- `expand --limit N` bounds each source separately: up to N provider ideas plus N unique autocomplete ideas, at most 2N. Default N is 20. Sixty is a caller-selected batch size, not a provider requirement, page quota, coverage guarantee or SEO threshold. Existing provider pins and spending caps still apply.
- Record chosen limits, returned counts by source, deduplication, on-topic accepted/rejected counts, omitted families and the reason to stop or widen. Never claim exhaustive coverage from a capped response. Autocomplete remains estimated until exact-phrase metrics are obtained; preserve provenance on duplicates.
- Reject off-topic broad matches even if they have high volume. Judge relevance against the brief's entity, jurisdiction, audience and reader decision. Do not silently use a global lexical filter that discards valid synonyms or adjacent intent.
- If the cap is reached and a plausible on-topic question family remains unexplored, use cached results, the free question-prefix sweep or a narrower seed first. Increase the per-source limit only where a specific missing family justifies the cost. Stop when additional sampling adds no actionable intent, coverage is sufficient, or the authorized budget is reached; record remaining uncertainty. Do not keep widening merely to hit a count or force a new page.
- Verify exact candidate metrics where available, the required SERP/PAA/question sweep, correct existing-page home, and duplicate/no-addition decisions. Missing paid-provider data follows the existing fallback rules, not a new failure gate.

Own background processes by their task ID/PID and wait/cancel only that task. Never use broad `pkill -f keyword_data.py` or terminate another routine's research. A command moved to background is still running; inspect its status before restarting work.

## Phase 4: audit rules against the actual result

Keep the existing independent reviewer and two-rework limit. For each affected route, record PASS, FAIL or justified N/A with artifact path/section and concrete evidence for:
1. Complete, current reviewer instructions and the writer's application map; site permission, stricter local exclusions and required professional review are preserved.
2. Reader question, exact-intent deduplication and no-addition branch. Do not force an experiment, conclusion or tool onto already sufficient content.
3. Source-to-claim traceability and actual basis: measured, calculated, modeled, client record, reported or unknown. Reproduce numerical claims and check counterexamples/conditions where applicable; retain a reasoning trail for non-numerical work.
4. Visible attribution beside the finding: what we did, the supported result, scope and a publishable way to inspect the method. Source-only work names the external source; private records remain private. No exact wording quota.
5. Intent-based takeaway (or existing sufficient verdict), agreement with the opening answer, table/tool and FAQs, and the condition or alternative that changes the recommendation. An honestly inconclusive answer may pass.
6. Testing eligibility separately from executed evidence; complete item coverage, real test dates, raw records and independent approval of the exact final content. Check title, metadata, byline, methods, picks and schema use one decision; inspect residual testing claims even when the badge is off. An unchanged migration snapshot is not a new test approval.
7. Selected visuals/tools match source outputs; test defaults/boundaries, accessibility and mobile readability. No mandatory calculator, screenshot or exact heading; no videos under the evidence contract.
8. Growth record and baseline/comparator status where the contribution requires them; unknown/unavailable is not zero and publishing is not proven uplift. Respect the terminal no-addition exemption.

Missing evidence for an applicable check is FAIL, not N/A. Recheck any changed reviewed artifact before publishing. At the existing publication gate, verify the audit's exact content/artifact hashes, current rules and required deployed source files; check built output, then verify live URLs after deployment. Never replace independent judgment with hashes or a fabricated PASS. Existing unchanged pages outside this run remain out of scope.

## Approval chart — completed preparation only

The approval chart is the gate to START content work. Present it only after all applicable preparation is complete and independently checked. Never show a ready-for-approval chart with “pending”, “not yet”, unchecked boxes or missing evidence. A failed preparation status may be shown only as a blocked readiness report with its specific failures, without asking for approval. If a prerequisite is unfinished, finish it before presenting the chart. If blocked, report the specific blocker without presenting a ready-for-approval chart. This does not authorize content generation, content edits or publication before Phase 0 approval.

Separate completed preparation from the execution plan:
- **Preparation summary:** show exactly ONE aggregate row: **Check / Result / Evidence** → **Preparation check / ✅ Passed / link to the full readiness report**. Pass requires every applicable underlying instruction/readiness check and independent review to be complete and evidenced. Keep the detailed read/application checklist and per-page checks in the linked run evidence; do not print the long checklist or repeat passed items in the on-screen chart. If any required check fails or lacks evidence, show **Preparation check / ❌ Failed — approval blocked / evidence link**, followed ONLY by the specific failures, affected targets and required fixes. No approval question until those failures are resolved. N/A decisions and their reasons stay in the detailed report, not as extra summary rows.
- **Execution plan:** retain the full original action table and Phases 1–9, including metadata, substantive writing, independent content audit, body updates, internal links, sitemap/IndexNow and commit/deploy/live verification. Use future action verbs and exact targets. These are the actions being approved, not completed-work checkboxes. Do not add a “pending” status column or label them passed.
- **Final results:** report actual completed execution/review/publication results after they occur. A blocked or failed run reports its actual issue; it does not display a partially complete approval chart or fabricate success.

Before showing the chart, read ALL applicable workflow instructions, including downstream writing, audit, linking and publication requirements. Use repeated `--instruction` arguments with `workflow-preflight.py prepare` to include those phase files in the build bundle; reuse already completed same-actor reading only when valid. The independent chart reviewer uses its own current instructions and verifies the preparation, not a fictitious Phase 4 content PASS.

Complete and evidence these preparation checks before the approval presentation:

| Preparation requirement | What must already be finished |
|---|---|
| Workflow freshness and full instruction reading | Verified startup; complete/current contracts, local rules and applicable phase instructions |
| Brief, scope and reader questions | Interpreted brief, exact reader questions, answer placement, formats and actionable targets |
| Keyword demand, relevance and discovery coverage | Saved real discovery results, correct provider/provenance, exact candidate checks, required SERP/PAA/question sweep and stop/widen rationale |
| Duplication and existing-page intent | Coverage lookup, checked commits, same-run overlap and independent duplicate-review decisions for every applicable target |
| Local testing eligibility and exclusions | Resolved per-page permission/exclusion decisions, including required professional-review obligations |
| Evidence and attribution preparation | Sources/reusable records inspected, actual evidence basis classified and a supported findings/attribution brief; no invented tests or benefits |
| Takeaway preparation | Planned intent-answering conclusion grounded in the research, material conditions and existing sufficient-verdict/no-addition decisions |
| Testing presentation preparation | Determine from actual available records whether TESTED can be proposed or the ordinary/excluded format is required; do not promise an unsupported label |
| Content standard and audit preparation | Required elements, depth/voice rules, source requirements and independent Phase 4 acceptance criteria incorporated in the brief |
| Tool/visual preparation | Useful medium chosen, inputs/sources/logic and feasibility assessed where applicable; actual implementation/audit remains in the approved execution plan |
| Internal-link preparation | Inspect source pages and relevant sections, specify inbound/outbound placements and targets, and confirm the required link coverage can be achieved |
| Technical SEO and publication preparation | Inspect applicable metadata/schema/canonical/sitemap/deployment wiring; define exact actions and live checks |
| Growth preparation | Read available outcomes; identify the applicable baseline/comparator/data status and hypothesis without claiming uplift; respect no-addition exemptions |
| Independent chart review | Final proposed rows, exclusions, research, readiness evidence and checklist verified by a distinct reviewer |
| Approval scope prepared | Explicit planned commit, push, live verification and IndexNow actions disclosed, or an explicit local-only scope; approval itself is the next user action, not a completed checklist row |

Show the same single aggregate preparation row in both the saved approval chart and on-screen presentation. Keep the complete underlying checklist in a separate linked run evidence report. Preserve the original action table, emerging clusters and exclusions; put the aggregate row under its own `## Preparation check` heading before the existing Phase 0 approval question. It cannot become an action row. When failed, show the specific failures as a blocked readiness report and do not present a ready chart or ask for approval. When passed, show no failure list or expanded checklist.

Maintain **Per-page preparation checks** in the linked readiness evidence (not as another visible checklist table on a passed chart): **Page / Duplicate check / Testing eligibility / Evidence and label decision / Takeaway brief / Evidence**. Every applicable preparation cell must have a verified decision and linked proof. Testing exclusions can pass preparation with the ordinary presentation explicitly selected; this never means a product test was performed. Do not include actual content-audit, implementation or live-deployment checkboxes in this pre-content table.

A preparatory testing decision does not approve final testing labels. After approval, Phase 3/4 still checks real run records, exact final content, independent approval, rendered methods/title/byline/schema and professional review as required. Likewise a planned takeaway is reviewed again against the actual generated page. No content is described as written, audited, built or live before those events occur.

Changed rules, targets or research invalidate the affected readiness decisions. Recheck them before presenting a revised approval chart. Imported charts must have their current preparation evidence revalidated. The independent chart reviewer rejects any missing preparation evidence, unsupported check mark or future execution result misrepresented as already complete. Preserve the sole Phase 0 human gate and all existing scope/exclusion/publication rules. This section supersedes older instructions to display unfinished status cells in an approval chart.

## Mandatory new-page briefs in the actual approval output

Every `create new content` action MUST have its own complete, visible brief under `## New-page briefs`, in BOTH the saved chart and the on-screen Phase 0 approval presentation. This applies to articles, comparisons, tools, downloads and every other new-page format. A URL/title row, a separate linked research file, a phase summary or a generic example does not substitute for the actual per-page brief. Do not shorten these briefs out of the approval output. Keep the existing action table, instruction checks, emerging clusters, exclusions, internal-link plan and full phase plan.

Give each brief a stable action-row identifier and exact target, matching the action table. Include all of the following with this run's actual researched decisions:

| Required detail | What the approval output must show |
|---|---|
| Identity | Action row ID, exact proposed URL, working H1/title, page type, format and medium; planned title/description where that metadata is in scope |
| Reader and answer | Intended audience, exact reader question, search intent, supported opening-answer brief and its section placement |
| Keyword evidence | Exact validated primary and supporting phrases, demand values/bands or honestly unavailable data, source/provenance, country/database and check date; no invented volumes |
| SERP and question findings | Actual competing result types/pages, relevant PAA/autocomplete questions, observed opportunity and material limits |
| Why a new page | Strongest existing-page matches with routes, why their reader intent does not already satisfy this question, checked commits and the independent duplicate-review decision |
| Planned outline | Specific section headings and the purpose/content of each section; planned FAQs drawn from research, required elements and the applicable local depth floor |
| Contribution and evidence | Supported finding/decision gap, planned original analysis or useful synthesis, evidence basis, exact inspected primary-source links/check dates and reusable record IDs where applicable |
| Tables, tools or visuals | Specific fields/comparisons, reader inputs and outputs, sourced assumptions and the format's purpose; justified N/A where none adds value |
| Testing and review | This site's permission/exclusion decision, actual available test-record references or ordinary/excluded presentation decision, truthful attribution wording and required professional-review obligations |
| Planned takeaway | The researched conclusion/answer, whom it applies to, material conditions/exceptions, and what would change it; preserve sufficient existing verdicts/no-addition decisions |
| Inbound internal links | Exact inspected source URLs and relevant source sections, proposed anchors, destination and the required inbound coverage |
| Outbound internal links | Exact relevant existing destination URLs, planned placement/anchor and reader purpose |
| Technical and measurement scope | Applicable canonical/schema/sitemap wiring, existing components/registries to reuse, measurement hypothesis and baseline/data availability; no claims of proven uplift |

Write concrete, page-specific decisions. A repeated generic template, placeholder headings, “research later”, omitted data provenance or links that have not been inspected do not satisfy preparation. Missing paid metrics may use the already authorized, clearly labeled fallback or honest unavailability; do not fabricate data to make a brief look complete. Missing support for a central claim requires narrowing/excluding the proposal rather than presenting an unfinished brief.

The independent chart reviewer must reconcile the action table and briefs one-to-one: every new-page action has a complete brief; every brief has a matching action; targets, keyword evidence, reader question, outline, testing decision, link placements and execution scope agree. Missing or mismatched briefs BLOCK the approval chart. Phase 0 repeats this check when loading an existing/imported chart and renders the full actual briefs before asking for approval. If output length requires multiple messages, show all completed sections before the single approval question; never substitute a shortened example or ask approval on a partial presentation.

After approval, Phase 3 consumes those exact approved briefs. Phase 4 verifies the generated content against them, and the existing later gates verify internal-link/technical/publication execution. Material changes to the proposed scope follow existing approval rules. Brief preparation is not a claim that the page has already been written, professionally reviewed, product-tested or published.

## Compact preparation display takes precedence

The single-row preparation summary supersedes older instructions to display Read/Followed columns or all preparation checks in the approval output. Detailed checking is still mandatory; only its presentation is condensed. Keep every actual new-page brief inline and complete, plus the original action chart, internal-link plan and full execution plan. A successful summary must link the detailed current evidence, never substitute a bare unsupported “passed”.

Fold legacy standalone duplicate-check pass rows into this one preparation summary. Keep the full independent duplicate-review result in the linked readiness evidence and the required existing-page rationale in each page brief. Do not print the aggregate row twice (once in the phase table and again in a separate checklist). Existing final gates accept the preparation-summary pass backed by the detailed duplicate-review evidence.

## Final rendered output and deployment closure

Read and apply `_rendered-page-audit.md` in full. Central answer/setup/availability research must be complete before preparation Passed. Audit complete rendered pages including inherited decision sections, injected copy, dates, schema and links after all planned transformations. Use the shared rendered capture/review/freshness/live comparison commands; changed output invalidates affected approval. Close verified deployment and measurement records. These are enforceable substeps of the existing gates, with no added phase or human approval.

For Mindmap, enforce `_mindmap-execution.md`: the reviewed structured manifest and `mindmap-gates.py` renderer produce the complete actual chart, its full per-page briefs and one preparation row. Raw/imported charts require revalidation; the writer blocks missing preparation/evidence before a paid call. Install the shared helper, tests and approved public case bank with this contract.

# Audit the complete rendered page

This contract applies to every routine that creates or changes website content, metadata, templates, injected sections, dates, internal links or structured data. It applies equally to local, global and cloud execution. It strengthens the existing independent audit and publication gates; it adds no phase or human approval.

## Prepare the answer before the approval chart

Finish research needed for the proposed answer, setup instructions, pricing, product availability, comparisons and takeaway before marking preparation Passed. “Fetch/verify in Phase 3” is unfinished preparation when the source supports the proposed answer. Optional unsupported material must be explicitly excluded from the approved scope, not presented as planned content with a future verification condition. Missing paid metrics may retain the authorized labeled fallback. Keep one preparation summary row and every complete new-page brief.

## Define the actual affected scope

Record every changed route and all routes affected by a shared template/helper, including affiliate, related-content, survey, attribution and date transformations. Enumerate these through the site's route registry or build output. A shared change is not confined to the example page that exposed it. Preserve unrelated content, exclusions, professional review and the existing no-addition branch. If a shared change affects a large set, mechanically inspect every affected route and independently review every distinct changed copy/template variant plus its source-support mapping. Record the complete route inventory and justify representative visual samples; never call a sample a full route check.

Prepare a JSON manifest with `author`, `canonicalBase`, and a nonempty `routes` array. Each route has `path`, optional `expectedUpdatedDate`, required on-page `requiredText` where useful, `forbiddenText` for the defects being repaired, and optional `growthFile`/`evidenceFile`. Use actual source dates rather than today's date for untouched pages. A route expected to carry an updated date must set `expectedUpdatedDate`; document genuine date-policy exceptions in the independent review.

## Existing Phase 4 audits the final candidate

1. Apply planned content, link edits and all reader-facing transformations before the final approval of affected pages. Monetization is content: an “append-only” map entry can add unreviewed prose and regress dates. Build/export or serve the candidate through the production rendering path. Never substitute a raw data object, generator draft or source grep for the rendered page.
2. Capture each complete rendered page with `.claude/tools/rendered-audit.py capture --manifest MANIFEST --base-url PREVIEW_OR_LIVE_BASE --out SNAPSHOT.json`. The helper saves HTML and readable text, metadata, links, structured data, dates and a semantic fingerprint. Static/server-rendered pages can use their complete HTTP HTML. For client-rendered pages, save the hydrated browser DOM to a directory named by route (`index.html` for `/`, otherwise `path/index.html`) and pass `--dom-dir`; also inspect the page in the browser. An empty app shell is not a page capture. Capture delivery must be complete: if the browser API caps long strings, return bounded chunks from one DOM snapshot together with its full length, join them outside the browser, and verify the returned length. Require actual parsed body and HTML closures; a truncation marker or a closing-tag string inside a script/comment does not prove completeness. Retain the complete raw HTML. Inspect responsive layout, tables and interactive behavior in the browser where applicable; record actual observations and evidence.
   Rotating third-party ads may use the helper's narrowly identified `volatileThirdPartyAds: "mediavine"` route option only when the independent review explicitly covers that normalization. The manifest binds the option to the review. Retain raw HTML and inspect real ad placement/overlap in browser evidence. Never exclude generic ad-like wrappers or first-party article text, reader-survey results, affiliate content, tested labels, bylines or structured data. Protected content inside an excluded region, an unverified wrapper or an unterminated region blocks capture. All other semantic content remains exact.
3. An independent reviewer who did not write the changes must read the entire rendered decision path, including inherited paragraphs, tables, FAQs, conclusions, injected copy, footer/disclaimers and visible labels. Contradictory or unsupported material affecting the revised answer is a blocker even when it predates the run. Unrelated historical style issues may remain advisory. Do not rewrite unrelated pages to satisfy a quota.
4. Audit all existing content/evidence/testing rules against the render. A vendor name or generic template cannot establish availability of an exact model in an editor, product integration, first-party app or paid plan. Verify the exact combination with a primary source or use useful conditional language with a direct availability link. Preserve relevant monetization and disclosures without claiming unsupported compatibility or popularity.
5. Verify the rendered visible updated date, pricing/disclaimer dates and JSON-LD against the intended source date. `dateModified` must never precede `datePublished`; injected content must never replace a newer date with an older constant. Sitemap lastmod follows the existing substantive-change policy; document legitimate link-only differences rather than stamping every page.
6. The reviewer saves a JSON review with `reviewer` (distinct from manifest `author`), `snapshotSha256`, and one result for every route: `fingerprint`, `verdict: PASS`, and evidence-backed `checks` for `wholePageCoherence`, `sourceSupport`, `testingAndAttribution`, `datesAndSchema`, `linksAndIndexability`, `renderedLayout`, and `scopeAndExclusions`. Each check is `{status: PASS|NA, evidence: concrete observation/artifact}`. NA needs a specific reason; the whole-page, source, date/schema, links and layout checks cannot be NA. The helper validates records, not reviewer understanding or factual truth. Never generate a review by filling PASS defaults.
7. Run `rendered-audit.py check --snapshot SNAPSHOT.json --review REVIEW.json --recapture`. Recapture uses the same actual preview/live origin and compares the current rendered fingerprints with the approved ones. For hydrated DOM, refresh the browser capture first; the independent reviewer must verify its freshness. A changed fingerprint, missing route/check, mechanical failure or same author/reviewer blocks publication. Every content/template/affiliate change after approval invalidates the affected page approval and requires recapture and independent review. Do not count a content rewrite as already approved because the underlying source record passed earlier.

## Existing publication gate verifies the live render

After the host deploys the intended revision, capture every affected live route and run `rendered-audit.py compare --approved PREVIEW_SNAPSHOT.json --live LIVE_SNAPSHOT.json --review REVIEW.json`. The complete semantic render must match the approved candidate; build IDs, script payloads and preview-origin URLs are excluded, but visible copy, metadata, links and JSON-LD are not. If rendering legitimately differs, independently review the live difference and correct the candidate; HTTP 200 alone is not success. Check actual host deployment evidence and preserve it with the commit ID. Submit IndexNow only for eligible verified live URLs under existing rules.

Close the measurement handoff with `rendered-audit.py record-deployment --snapshot LIVE_SNAPSHOT.json --approved PREVIEW_SNAPSHOT.json --review REVIEW.json --commit VERIFIED_COMMIT --deployment-evidence HOST_EVIDENCE.json --ledger reports/content-evidence.jsonl`. The host evidence must identify that commit and a successful live deployment. This updates manifest-linked growth records, recording the live verification, commit, evidence paths, baseline availability and first complete 28/56-day windows. Existing baselines are preserved; unavailable GSC stays explicitly unavailable with a retry reason, never zero or silently deferred. Reuse an already recorded first-live timestamp when refreshing a contribution. Do not claim SEO uplift from deployment, impressions, or an unelapsed window. Existing eligible routines perform later measurement; do not invent or alter schedules.

## Global and cloud installation

Install this sibling contract and `rendered-audit.py`/its regression tests with the shared workflow contracts into the active repository, preserving local rules. Read the full phase bundle and verify freshness in the checkout actually rendering/publishing the content. Cloud uses the published default branch; unpublished laptop files do not satisfy it. A read-only reviewer may write its own internal evidence files, but cannot modify the candidate content. Missing tooling, unavailable rendered output or a failed audit blocks the affected publication; resolve it within the authorized run.

Owner source/attribution clarification 2026-11-09: Within the existing independent review, test the central consequential conclusion against its strongest plausible primary-source counterexample. Source silence is not affirmative proof of a universal negative. Keep material product, use and applicability conditions in the first answer, FAQ and takeaway; a usual-use limitation must not become an unconditional claim about every product. Record this in the existing sourceSupport/consequentialClaims evidence, without an extra pass or review tier.

Audit the complete rendered attribution, including unchanged templates, bylines, footer promises and author schema. An inherited “Tested and reviewed by” or “tested guidance” claim cannot have testingAndAttribution=NA. A PASS must explain the actual permitted test evidence/identity or truthful third-party attribution. If that evidence does not exist, remove or narrow the unsupported label; do not invent a person, credentials, testing, or a PASS. Metadata-only corrections retain their existing scope; no unrelated product research or new physical testing is required merely to remove a false badge.

## Authorized unattended Mindmap: continue through publication

For local, global and cloud Mindmap runs, resolve execution authority from the actual saved routine or caller before Phase 0. An explicitly authorized end-to-end publishing routine (including the existing `*-auto` callers) uses automatic Phase 0 authorization within its saved site, topic, spending and publication scope. A schedule or cloud environment alone is not authorization. Record the caller/source and authorized scope in the existing run notes; retain the complete independently reviewed chart and explicit `publicationScope`. Never invent approval, broaden permissions, change schedules or enable paused jobs. For an authorized unattended run, save the complete chart, record that existing authorization, and proceed through Phases 1–9 without a confirmation question. Manual runs retain the existing Phase 0 human gate. This scoped rule takes precedence over generic instructions to wait at Phase 0 or stop the whole Mindmap run after one page exhausts rework.

The deterministic chart's `status: ready-for-approval` describes completed preparation. Accept it after `validate-chart` succeeds and the required manual or existing unattended authorization is recorded separately. Do not wait for a nonexistent `ready-for-execution` mutation or edit the generated chart to invent approval. A changed plan requires independent revalidation; changes within existing unattended authorization do not require another human gate. Exclude changes outside that authorization.

**Recover automatically, then continue with publishable work.** Finish missing briefs, source checks, duplicate decisions, evidence records and internal-link plans before preparation PASS. For a failed page, apply the existing remediation ladder: mechanical fixes, targeted fixes and up to two substantive reworks per page, with fresh independent review of changed output. Keep valid reviews of unchanged pages. Execute relevant accessible analysis during the run; missing historical test logs do not require owner input. If quantitative analysis adds no value or lacks defensible inputs, use the already permitted, justified source-based answer and truthful labels. When an optional asset or evidence source is unavailable, choose a feasible useful presentation within scope, revise/revalidate its brief, and audit the result. Never replace a central promised deliverable with an unfinished specification. Optional surveys, case matches, numerical analysis and unavailable measurement baselines do not create an extra publication gate; record the real limitation, never fake records, respondents, numbers or PASS results. A source essential to the central answer remains required.

**Isolate unresolved pages.** In an authorized unattended Mindmap run, if a page still fails after its allowed repairs, mark that page deferred with its concrete findings and continue the independently passing pages. Remove only this run's failed-page changes, tentative routes, links and sitemap/schema references before building the publishable subset. Preserve unrelated local/staged work; never reset an entire file containing someone else's changes. Rebuild and independently review any page or shared output changed by this isolation. A shared template, source-freshness, build, rendering, deployment, access or mandatory professional-review failure affects every page that depends on it; repair it or withhold that dependency group. Do not publish unreviewed, broken or prohibited material to claim completion. If safe isolation cannot be established, retain the affected group for follow-up while completing any independent work. This exception changes the scope of escalation for unattended Mindmap only; manual runs and other routines keep their existing stop rules.

Commit/push the passing subset within existing authorization, verify the exact reviewed output live, and submit only verified eligible URLs to IndexNow using the existing process. If all candidates are already covered or deferred, finish with an accurate no-publication outcome rather than wait indefinitely or manufacture a page. Retain an internal per-route record of published, deferred and failed outcomes plus reasons; use only the caller's already authorized reporting channel. Never claim a deferred page passed or was published. Preserve local exclusions, professional review, models, budgets, credentials and the no-addition branch. Routine quality checks are automatic repair work; they do not add owner confirmation stops.

# Executable Mindmap preparation, evidence and delivery

These are enforced substeps of the existing chart, Phase 3 and Phase 4. Keep the existing Phase 0 approval, local exclusions, schedules, model pins and publication permissions. No additional human gate. Global commands install this contract, `.claude/tools/mindmap-gates.py`, its tests and `_approved-cases.json` in the active repository alongside the checkpoint/rendered-audit dependencies. Never replace a site's `_experience.md` or testing permission with Layer3's.

## 1. Produce the actual approval chart from a reviewed manifest

Use `<RUN>/approval-manifest.json` with `schemaVersion: 1`, the original stable `jobId` (retain it on resume), `author`, actual local `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `source`, `interpretedBrief`, `chartPath` (the actual `<CHART>` path), and:

- `actions`: the full original action rows. Every row contains `id`, `problem`, `solution`, `bucket`, `target`, `format`, `best_medium`, `resolved_deliverable`, `serp_verdict`, `serp_evidence`, `reader_question`, `answer`, `answer_placement`. Buckets are `consolidation advisory`, `update existing metadata`, `create new content`, `update existing body text`, `add internal links`. Keep consolidation advisory only.
- `newPageBriefs`: exactly one per new-content action, matching `actionId` and exact `target`. Required fields: `identity`, `readerAndAnswer`, `keywordEvidence`, `serpAndQuestions`, `whyNewPage`, `outline`, `contributionAndEvidence`, `tablesToolsVisuals`, `testingAndReview`, `takeaway`, `inboundLinks`, `outboundLinks`, `technicalAndMeasurement`, plus `evidenceFiles`.
- `identity` contains the working `title`, `pageType`, `format`, `medium` and any planned metadata in scope. Its format must equal the action format and its medium must equal the resolved deliverable. `readerAndAnswer` contains `question`, `answer`, `placement`, copied exactly from the corresponding action fields (including question-evidence tags), plus the audience/intent detail. `outline` is a nonempty array of specific headings and purposes. Other briefs retain all the actual detail required by `_workflow-checkpoints.md`; filling generic strings does not pass independent review.
- `inboundLinks` contains `required` (this site's real required count, at least one) and `placements`; `outboundLinks` contains `placements`. Each placement has exact local `source`, `target`, `section`, `anchor`, `purpose` and `inspection` artifact. Preserve stricter site coverage. An honestly empty outbound plan needs `notApplicableReason`. Link inspections happen before approval.
- `preparation`: `{status: "PASS", readiness: {path, sha256}}`, pointing to the completed detailed readiness report. `evidenceFiles` lists the inspected source/research artifacts. Every artifact reference is `{path, sha256}`, relative to the active repository, with the current actual file hash. Per-page references may reuse the same inspected source.
- `emergingClusters`, `exclusions` and `executionPlan`: retain the original clusters, exceptions and all Phases 1–9. Each execution entry is `{phase: 1..9, action: <specific future action>}`. These are planned actions, never claimed completed work.
- `publicationScope`: explicit booleans `commit`, `push`, `liveVerification`, `indexNow`, matching the actual authorization being requested or the existing authorized local-only scope. Do not broaden it.

The existing independent chart reviewer checks the complete manifest, source research, local rules, coverage, evidence and every brief. It writes `<RUN>/chart-review.json`: `reviewer` distinct from `author`, `verdict: "PASS"`, `jobId` exactly matching the manifest, canonical `manifestSha256`, actual file `readinessSha256`, and concrete `evidence` describing its review. Use `mindmap-gates.py hash --file <file>` to calculate hashes. A hash or helper return is not independent judgment. Never fabricate a review or populate PASS defaults.

```bash
python3 .claude/tools/mindmap-gates.py render-chart --manifest <RUN>/approval-manifest.json --review <RUN>/chart-review.json --out <CHART>
python3 .claude/tools/mindmap-gates.py validate-chart --manifest <RUN>/approval-manifest.json --review <RUN>/chart-review.json
```

Present the complete generated chart, including every actual brief and link placement, unchanged. If long, show it in complete bounded parts before the sole approval question. The renderer provides exactly one preparation summary row. A failed command means a blocked readiness report with specific failures, never an approval-ready chart. Do not hand-render a shortened substitute. Revalidate imported/old Markdown charts by reconstructing their actual supported manifest; do not grandfather missing briefs or invent missing research. Changed sources, readiness or scope invalidate the affected review. No-addition charts may have empty action/brief arrays with their real explanation and do not request pointless content approval. Automatic revalidation of an already-approved unchanged scope adds no human gate. Preserve the original 12 action-column positions, appended row IDs, date frontmatter and `## Emerging search patterns (clusters)` heading. Non-content rows retain explicit N/A fields and exact file-or-route targets; body rows retain N/A format/medium fields but still require actual reader intent and an exact route. The writer also checks that the actual saved chart exactly matches the complete deterministic rendering.

## 2. Execute relevant analysis before the writer

Choose the method that improves the actual reader decision. Run accessible calculations/modeling when meaningful; records are outputs of the run, not a demand that the owner supply a historical test log. A useful model starts from supported public facts, explicit assumptions and a decision-changing condition. Estimates need defensible inputs/ranges. Never derive actual product accuracy, operating success or customer savings from unrelated public benchmarks.

Do not force calculations. For a combat drone with undisclosed price/performance, for example, use verified public facts, useful comparisons, unknowns and the limits of any defensible estimate. If there is no defensible estimate, explain that in the internal record and narrow the answer. News, definitions, qualitative comparisons and already sufficient pages may require no numerical work. Preserve medical/psychedelic/professional exclusions and required human professional review. A source-based or inconclusive answer can pass; arbitrary arithmetic cannot create value. The existing no-addition branch remains terminal and skips writing, tool building and numerical/growth work unless another real experiment needs them.

Before assembling closed facts, retrieve the relevant approved client/fleet records:

```bash
python3 .claude/tools/mindmap-gates.py cases --query "<exact approved reader_question, including its internal evidence tag>" --publisher <active-site-domain> --out <RUN>/evidence/<slug>/cases.json
```

This reads the active site's full `_experience.md` plus the shared approved bank, preserving source IDs, exact quotes, ownership and attribution limits. It does not grant another site Layer3's history or testing permission. Record selected/rejected matches and why; never force a client mention. Additional accessible approved records can be added with their source, precise public-use scope and supported facts; a client list alone does not establish outcomes. Keep private records private. Update the shared bank through the existing reviewed sync when approved source facts change. For Layer3, also run the existing durable reader-survey catalog/facts lookup every Phase 3 run. No completed survey is not zero demand; do not simulate respondents or require waiting for a new survey.

Extend the existing `evidence/<slug>/evidence.json` with `gateSchemaVersion: 1`, `author`, `route`, `readerQuestion`, `decisionGap`, actual `finding`, `conditions`, `whatWouldChange`, `basis`, `sourceArtifacts` (artifact references alongside the existing source URLs/check dates), `caseSelection` (the retrieval artifact reference) and `caseDecisions` (actual selections/rejections and reasons).

- `basis: calculated|modeled`: include `method`, `units`, `limitations`, `counterexample`, and `execution: {command: [actual executable and arguments], code: {path, sha256}, inputs: [{path, sha256}], output: {path, sha256}}`. Execute the reviewed code, save machine-readable JSON results and retain all sourced inputs/assumptions. Fixed seeds are required where relevant. Do not merely copy arithmetic into a report and claim a saved executable run.
- `basis: measured`: include method, units, limitations, counterexample and actual `runs: [{testedAt, scope, artifact: {path, sha256}}]`. Existing relevant verified owner/product records are reusable. Physical or stochastic product tests do not need identical fresh API responses. Preserve the separate testing-label adapter's exact full-coverage/approval requirements.
- `basis: reported|client-record`: retain `whyNoQuantitativeAnalysis` and the actual `reasoning` from sources to conclusion. A useful non-numerical synthesis or relevant documented case can pass. Do not imply an executed product test.

The packet reader question and case-retrieval query must match the approved action.reader_question exactly, including its internal question-evidence tag. If that string changes, rerun deterministic case retrieval and refresh caseSelection and affected artifact hashes together before writer dispatch. Keep the tag internal; public reader questions and copy contain no workflow labels. Keep the existing source URLs, provenance, takeaway, survey and applicable growth fields. These gate fields extend the current packet; they do not create a second evidence system. If the page needs a claim the sources cannot support, narrow/exclude it rather than manufacturing numbers.

Mindmap `content_gen.py write`, `section` and `fix` calls require:

```text
--mindmap-manifest <RUN>/approval-manifest.json --mindmap-review <RUN>/chart-review.json --analysis-packet <RUN>/evidence/<slug>/evidence.json
```

The shared writer checks these before spending a call when caller/path identifies Mindmap. Do not relocate prompts or change caller names to bypass it. The target must match the manifest and packet. This verifies preparation/evidence structure, not Phase 0 human approval or a final content PASS; the existing permissions and independent review remain mandatory.

## 3. Existing Phase 4 verifies usefulness, reproducibility and the render

First judge whether the finding resolves the approved reader decision beyond a rewrite of sources. Reject trivial arithmetic used as an originality claim, unsupported assumptions, missing material conditions, or an asset that adds no value. Accept relevant non-numerical reasoning and justified no-addition decisions.

For calculations/modeling, inspect code and inputs, independently rerun the safe deterministic calculation, and save fresh JSON output to a distinct reviewer artifact (never the original output or an alias). Compare its results, units, boundary cases and counterexample to the exact article. Do not execute unreviewed code or spend on unnecessary repeat product/API runs. For measured work, inspect actual raw task records and independently verify the scoring/claims; do not demand identical stochastic outputs. For source-only/client work, verify the reasoning and exact approved public scope.

Perform the existing complete rendered-page audit after all content, asset, template, affiliate and link transformations. Save the normal rendered snapshot and independent rendered review. In the analysis review JSON retain `reviewer`, `verdict: "PASS"`, canonical `packetSha256`, and `{status: "PASS", evidence: <concrete observation>}` for `usefulness`, `sourceAndAssumptions`, `conditionsAndCounterexample`, `renderedConsistency`, `localExclusions`. Include file-hashed `renderedSnapshot` and `renderedReview` references from that same reviewer. Quantitative replays also include canonical `replaySha256`.

```bash
python3 .claude/tools/mindmap-gates.py audit-analysis --packet <RUN>/evidence/<slug>/evidence.json --review <RUN>/audit/<slug>-analysis.json --replay-output <RUN>/audit/<slug>-replay.json
```

Omit `--replay-output` for measured/source/client work without a deterministic calculation. Independently check any numerical derived claims separately. This gate supplements the existing `rendered-audit.py check/compare` and does not replace them. Missing evidence is a failure; changed outputs invalidate affected approvals. Keep the existing rework limit and publication/live-verification process.

The terminal no-addition branch needs no new rendered capture, product run, asset, numerical packet or growth registration. Its existing evidence-backed independent chart decision suffices. If explicitly checking a saved no-addition note with this helper, use `basis: no-addition`, `author`, `route`, `readerQuestion`, `whyNoAddition`, `existingAnswer: {path, sha256}` and an independent `noAddition: {status: PASS, evidence}` decision bound to that note; the helper returns before render/replay requirements.

## 4. Finish the selected useful asset in the approved run

Use prose, a finite table, SVG, a genuine screenshot, an image/illustration, downloadable data or an interactive tool when that format improves the answer and available capabilities support it. Reuse components. Generated illustrations never prove product use. Build and audit the actual asset and its page within Phase 3/4; no placeholder, spec-only completion or future-human-build branch. Determine feasibility before the chart; narrow or exclude an infeasible asset while retaining a supported useful answer. Do not force an asset or add another URL for existing intent. Videos remain outside this Mindmap evidence workflow.
# Keyword demand ladder — NEVER block a routine on a dry API key

<!-- keyword-discovery-bounds-v1 -->
**Discovery limits:** `expand --limit N` returns up to N provider ideas PLUS N unique autocomplete ideas (at most 2N, default N=20). This is a per-source batch bound, not a chart/page quota or coverage guarantee. Keep existing provider pins and spending caps. Save raw outputs; filter off-topic matches before ranking, validate exact shortlisted phrases, and record counts by source, rejected topics and the stop/widen reason. If relevant families remain unexplored, prefer free question-prefix mining or narrower seeds before raising the limit. The existing chart reviewer checks these artifacts under `_workflow-checkpoints.md`. Never terminate other runs with a broad process-name kill; use this run's task ID/PID.
<!-- /keyword-discovery-bounds-v1 -->


**Standing rule (applies to EVERY pass that needs keyword volume/difficulty):
a routine must never stop, skip, or email failure because a keyword API key is
missing, expired, or out of credits.** Demote one rung and keep going.

## The ladder — SEMRUSH FIRST, with ranked backups

**USER RULE 2026-11-02: SEMRUSH is the primary keyword tool wherever it can
answer; DataForSEO is primary only for what SEMRUSH does not have (live SERPs
with titles/snippets, People Also Ask text, AI Overview citations, long-tail
phrases SEMRUSH does not track).** Ahrefs units are reserved for site audits,
so Ahrefs is last. The best **usable** provider wins each field for the whole run:

| Field | Order | Why this order |
|---|---|---|
| **volume** | `semrush` → `dataforseo` → `ahrefs` | SEMRUSH `phrase_these` (10 units/keyword, prepaid). DataForSEO `keyword_overview` only when SEMRUSH has no key, no units, or errors. |
| **kd** | `semrush` → `dataforseo` → `ahrefs` | SEMRUSH KDI (`phrase_kdi`, 50 units/keyword). DataForSEO Labs KD is modeled; fallback only. |
| **expand** | `semrush` → `dataforseo` → `ahrefs` | SEMRUSH `phrase_related` + `phrase_questions` (dedicated questions report). |
| **ranked keywords / competitors / movers** | `semrush` → `dataforseo` | `scripts/lib/semrush.py` (`domain_organic`, `domain_organic_organic`, `display_positions`) behind `dfs_keyword_gap.py` and `dfs_winner_loser.py`. |
| **vendor roster for head keywords** | `semrush` → `dataforseo` | SEMRUSH `phrase_organic` top 10 (no titles); a keyword SEMRUSH does not track falls back to the live SERP. |
| **SERP** | `dataforseo` only | No other vendor sells live SERP with PAA text and AI Overview citations at any price. Not a ladder — see `scripts/lib/serp.py`. |
| **technical site audit** | `ahrefs` → `dataforseo` | Ahrefs' crawler sees what a page alone cannot (backlink-driven issues, crawl depth, orphan pages). DataForSEO OnPage covers every issue the auto-fix table can act on, at ~$0.00015/URL — see `scripts/lib/site_audit.py`, which emits **Ahrefs' issue slugs** so nothing downstream changes. |

**One provider per field, for the whole run.** Every row's volume comes from one
vendor and every row's KD comes from one vendor, so rows stay comparable to each
other. Different fields may come from different vendors — a row can carry Ahrefs
KD next to DataForSEO volume, and both `source` (volume) and `kd_source` are
stamped on it. What is forbidden is two vendors' volumes inside one chart.

**Google Autocomplete is NOT a rung — it ALWAYS runs, on top.** It is free,
keyless and live, so it adds to every call regardless of which provider
answered: `expand()` merges its suggestions into the provider's ideas, and
`volumes()` attaches an `autocomplete: {completions, corroborates}` signal to
every row. Phrases no provider has data for still fall back to a conservative
autocomplete BAND labelled `source: estimate`. Disable only with
`AUTOCOMPLETE_ENRICH=0`; cap corroboration with `AUTOCOMPLETE_ENRICH_CAP`
(default 80 rows).

A provider is skipped automatically on `ERROR 132 :: API UNITS BALANCE IS ZERO`,
`API units limit reached`, HTTP 401/402/403, or a missing key — the exact
condition that killed the podcast-pain runs on 2026-08-18, and the condition
Ahrefs and SEMRUSH are BOTH in as of 2026-08-23.

### The rule generalizes beyond keywords

This file is named for keyword demand because that is where it started, but the
standing rule is about **vendors, not fields**: no routine in this fleet ends
because one vendor's meter ran out. When you add a data source to any routine,
give it a rung below and a way to say which rung answered.

Two corollaries learned the hard way:

- **A check that did not run is not a pass.** A fallback with narrower coverage
  must report what it could not see (`unavailable_on_this_source`), never let a
  silent omission read as a clean bill of health.
- **Normalize at the source, not downstream.** `site_audit.py` translates
  DataForSEO's checks into Ahrefs' issue slugs inside the helper, so the fix
  table, gates and email are untouched. Compare the winner/loser pass, whose two
  Ahrefs sources need a field-mapping table in the skill itself — that mapping is
  a cost you pay on every future edit.

### DataForSEO specifics

Keys: `$DATAFORSEO_LOGIN` + `$DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD`, or the pre-encoded
`$DATAFORSEO_B64`. Pay-as-you-go against a prepaid balance, so unlike a metered
monthly allowance it does not hit a cliff mid-month. Two controls, neither
needing a code change: `DFS_ENABLED=0` removes it from every field ladder, and
`DFS_MAX_COST_USD` (default `$2.00`) caps per-process spend — on hitting the cap
the field demotes to the next provider instead of spending on.

### Pinned order — `KEYWORD_PROVIDERS`

Set `KEYWORD_PROVIDERS` (comma list, e.g. `semrush,dataforseo`) to replace the
per-field order above for every field; a provider left off the list is never called.
**/mindmap-pass always runs with `KEYWORD_PROVIDERS=semrush,dataforseo`** (never
Ahrefs, USER RULE 2026-10-20; SEMRUSH first, USER RULE 2026-11-02). An older pin of
just `dataforseo` is widened to `semrush,dataforseo` by the helper itself
(`SEMRUSH_ENABLED=0` turns that off). If both are down or capped, the run falls to
the labelled autocomplete estimate, not to Ahrefs.

## How to call it — always through the shared helper

`scripts/lib/keyword_data.py` implements the whole ladder (stdlib only, no pip).
**Do not hand-roll a SEMRUSH or Ahrefs call in a phase.** **Never hardcode a key
into a committed file.** Keys resolve exactly like every other key in the fleet
(same pattern as `.claude/scripts/bing_webmaster.py`): environment variable
first, then `.claude/routines.config`, then `~/.claude/secrets.env`. Cloud
routines pass `SEMRUSH_API_KEY` / `AHREFS_API_KEY` inline from the trigger
config — a routine whose trigger has no `AHREFS_API_KEY` yet simply runs one
rung lower, on public-source estimates, instead of failing.

From Python:

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts/lib")
from keyword_data import volumes, expand, passes_floor, score_volume, notes
rows  = volumes(["invoice automation", "dental crm"])   # dict keyed by lowercase phrase
ideas = expand("invoice automation", limit=20)          # related/matching terms
```

From a shell (for phases that shell out):

```bash
python3 scripts/lib/keyword_data.py volumes --phrase "x" --phrase "y"
python3 scripts/lib/keyword_data.py expand  --seed "x" --limit 20
python3 scripts/lib/keyword_data.py status   # which rungs are live right now
```

Every row comes back in one shape regardless of provider, carrying `source`
(the VOLUME provider), `kd_source` (the KD provider — may differ), `confidence`,
`volume`, `volume_low`, `volume_high`, `kd`, `cpc` (USD), and `autocomplete`
(`{completions, corroborates}` — always present unless enrichment is disabled).

`status` prints which provider won each field this run:

```json
{"selected": {"volume": "dataforseo", "kd": "dataforseo", "expand": "dataforseo"}}
```

## Honesty rules — non-negotiable

The point of rung 3 is to keep shipping, **not** to launder a guess into a fact.

1. **Never present an estimate as measured volume.** An estimate row is a band
   (`est. 150-1500/mo`), always written with its source: `estimate — Google
   Autocomplete, NOT measured`.
2. **Charts must carry the source column.** Any chart/table row built on rung 3
   states `source: estimate (autocomplete)` in its evidence cell. A reader must
   be able to tell measured demand from inferred demand at a glance.
3. **Rank measured above estimated.** When both exist, a real-volume row
   outranks an estimated row of nominally similar size.
4. **Floors use `passes_floor(row, floor)`** from the helper — never a raw
   `row["volume"] >= floor` comparison. Measured rows score their real volume;
   estimate rows score their band MIDPOINT, because scoring estimates at the low
   end would fail nearly every row in an all-estimate run and quietly recreate
   the blocked-routine failure.
5. **Say which provider won each field.** Every routine email/digest includes a
   line like `Keyword data: volume=dataforseo, kd=dataforseo (Ahrefs units
   exhausted, SEMRUSH 403)`. `keyword_data.notes()` returns exactly that log. A
   run that silently degrades is a bug.
6. **Do not over-read DataForSEO KD.** It is modeled, not calibrated against a
   link graph. Nothing in this fleet gates on KD — `passes_floor()` scores
   volume only — so treat a DataForSEO KD as a rough ordering hint, never as a
   reason to drop a row.
7. **Read DataForSEO volume as a bucket, not a count.** Google rounds Keyword
   Planner volumes and merges close variants, so cluster totals are more
   trustworthy than any single row.
8. **Still never invent a keyword.** The ladder relaxes where the *numbers* come
   from. Phrases themselves must always be real (autocomplete, GSC, the brief,
   the SERP) — fabricating queries remains forbidden at every rung.

This is Step 1 of `/mindmap-pass`. It replaces seo-gsc-pass's "build chart from 5 GSC screenshots" step. Instead of reading GSC keyword screenshots, it reads **whatever the user handed you** — free text, an image, a chart/screenshot of data, a pasted news article, a URL, or a half-formed "here's a thought" — interprets it into concrete topics the user wants on the site, **validates and expands that intent through the keyword demand ladder (best available provider PER FIELD, plus Google Autocomplete on top of every call)**, reads the LIVE SERP for the surviving cluster heads, clusters the demand, and produces the **same machine-readable chart** the rest of the phases (0–9) consume unchanged.

Run this phase **only when** Phase 0 cannot find a chart at `reports/mindmap-pass/<TODAY>.md`. If today's chart already exists, or the user passed a chart path argument, skip this phase and let Phase 0 load it.

This phase produces the file Phase 0 then loads. Once it is saved, control returns to Phase 0 for selection, staleness check, parsing, and the manifest gate.

## The input can be ANYTHING — capture it first, do not ask for GSC data
Unlike `/seo-gsc-pass`, this workflow does **not** want GSC screenshots. Its input is the user's own brief about what they want added to the site. Accept and handle every input modality present in the current conversation:

- **Free text / a "random thought"** — e.g. "I think we should own the 'AI receptionist for dental offices' angle." Treat the text as the statement of intent; extract the topics, entities, audiences, and angles inside it.
- **An image** — read it. A **photo/screenshot of a whiteboard, slide, or notes** → OCR/transcribe the concepts. A **chart or data screenshot** (e.g. a trend graph, a competitor's traffic table, a keyword list) → read the axes/labels/rows and pull out the themes and any entities named. A **product/marketing screenshot** → identify what product or topic it depicts.
- **A pasted news article or URL** — extract the story's entities, claims, and the emerging theme; treat "what would a searcher look up after reading this?" as the seed set. If it's a bare URL and fetching is available, fetch it; otherwise work from the text the user pasted.
- **A collection / cluster the user typed** — e.g. a list of topics or keywords. Treat each as a seed.
- **A mix** — e.g. an image plus a sentence of context. Merge them into one intent.

**If NO input is present** (no text beyond the bare command, no image, no article) AND no chart exists → **STOP** and ask the user to paste the text / attach the image / drop the article or link describing what they want added. Do NOT invent a brief.

Write a short **Interpreted brief** paragraph at the top of your working notes (and later into the saved chart's frontmatter/source line): 2–4 sentences restating, in your own words, what the user wants added — the topics, the audience, the angle, and the input modality it came from. This is what everything downstream is validated against; if your interpretation is wrong, the user catches it at the Phase 0 manifest gate.

## API key (read from environment — NEVER embed in this file or the saved chart)
- **DATA SOURCE IS SEMRUSH, THEN DATAFORSEO — USER RULES 2026-10-20 + 2026-11-02, overrides every provider line below.** This pass never uses Ahrefs (no Ahrefs API, no Ahrefs MCP). Prefix EVERY `scripts/lib/keyword_data.py` call with `KEYWORD_PROVIDERS=semrush,dataforseo` (in Python, set `os.environ["KEYWORD_PROVIDERS"] = "semrush,dataforseo"` before the first call), so volume, KD and expansion come from SEMRUSH first and DataForSEO only when SEMRUSH has no key, no units or errors. The SEMRUSH reports this file names (`phrase_these`, `phrase_kdi`, `phrase_related`, `phrase_fullsearch`, `phrase_questions`) are what `volumes()` / `expand()` call — never hand-roll them. Live SERP / PAA / AI Overview comes from `scripts/lib/serp.py` (DataForSEO — SEMRUSH has no live SERP). If both are unavailable or capped, the helper drops to the labelled autocomplete estimate — never to Ahrefs. Check with `KEYWORD_PROVIDERS=semrush,dataforseo python3 scripts/lib/keyword_data.py status` (ahrefs must read `off`).
- **Keyword demand comes from the shared ladder, not a single API.** Call `scripts/lib/keyword_data.py` (`volumes()` / `expand()`), which picks the best usable provider for each field automatically (pinned to SEMRUSH then DataForSEO for this pass — see the rule above) and always adds live Google Autocomplete on top. Read `.claude/commands/_keyword-demand-ladder.md` before this phase. Do NOT hand-roll a SEMRUSH call and do NOT hardcode a key — the helper reads `$SEMRUSH_API_KEY` and `$DATAFORSEO_B64` (or `$DATAFORSEO_LOGIN` / `$DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD`) from the environment (`us` database by default; override with `SEMRUSH_DATABASE`).
- **Do not over-read DataForSEO KD or volume (fallback rows, `source: dataforseo`).** Its KD is modeled, not link-graph calibrated; its volume comes from Google but is rounded into buckets with close variants merged. Trust cluster totals over single rows, and never drop a row on a DataForSEO KD alone.
- **DataForSEO controls:** `DFS_ENABLED=0` removes it from every ladder; `DFS_MAX_COST_USD` (default `$2.00`) caps per-process spend, demoting the field rather than overspending. (GSC performance data may still be consulted later, in the execution phases' metadata gates — that is a separate signal, not keyword discovery.)
- **NEVER stop this pass because a key is missing or dry.** The helper demotes a rung and continues. If a phrase has no provider volume, keep going and label that row `source: estimate (autocomplete) — NOT measured`, carrying the band rather than a point figure. Apply floors with `passes_floor()`, and state the rung that ran in the summary (`keyword_data.notes()`). Fabricating a volume number, or inventing a keyword phrase, remains forbidden at every rung.
- If you must call SEMRUSH from a shell, prefix so the key never lands in shell history/logs (e.g. `SEMRUSH_API_KEY="$SEMRUSH_API_KEY" python scripts/semrush_ai_seo_research.py ...`).

## API budget discipline (SEMRUSH costs credits — use it moderately)
Be deliberately economical; do not hammer the API.
- **One pull per seed / phrase.** Expand each seed once (`phrase_related` / `phrase_fullsearch` / `phrase_questions`), validate each candidate once (`phrase_these` for volume/CPC, `phrase_kdi` for difficulty). Batch phrases with `;` joins (both `phrase_these` and `phrase_kdi` accept a `;`-separated `phrase` list) instead of one call per keyword.
- **Only look up metrics for real candidates**, not every raw expansion result. Filter to plausible, on-mission phrases first, then validate that shortlist.
- **Keep the seed set tight** (a handful of seeds derived from the brief). Cache intermediate JSON/CSV under `reports/mindmap-pass/` and read from it instead of re-querying.
- Prefer free signals (the Autocomplete tool, web search, the codebase, the target-keyword doc) for judgment calls; spend SEMRUSH credits only where a real metric is needed.
